text.p: Copper prices veered lower during late Thursday LME trading and with spread backwardations also softening the market notched up a poor technical close, ending at its lows, traders said.
In Chicago, the Commodities Research Bureau Index was 1.92 points higher at 243.29.

In London, copper traders said business was patchy, and once it became obvious that the market was not going to clear $2,215/2,200 - an area it has faltered at recently - declines started to accelerate. Below $2,200, selling picked up, and the end of the kerb three months was trading at $2,179, down $29 from yesterday's kerb and just above a key long-term indicator. Cash/threes was at $150/155, some $15 softer.

Aluminium attempted to push higher, with some traders citing good spot physical interest this week. However, the market was baulked by copper's trend. "I see that copper is down, which means that aluminium will follow," one said. Prices managed to stabilise above $1,520, and finished at $, a $ loss from the previous kerb.

Lead was content to hold just above $690, and closed at that level, up $2 from the previous kerb. Zinc drifted lower, however, even though there have been a clutch of mine closures and cutbacks recently. Last trade was at $1,065, down $4.
There was little movement in the nickel market throughout the session, with prices ending the day at $6,880 a tonne, a $65 loss from yesterday.
Tin also fell away, although the extent of the setback was fairly small with the market holding close to the $6,100 level. Last business was at $6,090, a $25 loss.
The alloy market was generally neglected, and closed at $1,360/65 a tonne, against Wednesday's level of $1,375.

CBOT wheat futures were mixed at midsession with nearby December higher on talk that most of the wheat posted Thursday for delivery on that month was stopped by domestic mills, traders said. Traders said there was talk Egypt on Saturday would tender for 300,000 to 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin wheat, and there were hopes the U.S. may land some of the business. But U.S. exporters were skeptical the U.S. would realize any of the business and said Egypt probably would be in the market for only slightly more than 50,000 tonnes, the amount for which that country said it was inviting bids. At 1130 CST, wheat was 2-1/4 cents higher to three cents lower, with December up 2-1/4 at $3.80-1/2 p

CSCE world sugar futures set their nine-point trading range early and floated quietly above unchanged through the close as values consolidated recent losses, market sources said. The spot month closed 0.01 firmer at 10.31 cents, traded 10.39 to 10.30. The back months finished 0.02 to 0.05 higher.

New York precious metals futures remained lower but steady at midday after recovering from opening lows, following reportedly heavy selling in gold in Asia and Europe overnight. COMEX February gold was down 80 cents at $371.70 midday, after recovering from an early low at $369.50, with resistance still seen around $373.50. In the bullion market, spot gold was quoted $369.70/370.20 an ounce, compared to the London Thursday afternoon fix at $369.00, and the New York close Wednesday around $370.70/371.20.

U.S. crudes were comfortably marking gains in mid-afternoon trading Thursday, supported by advances in NYMEX products futures and technically positive crude futures, traders said. Crude traders said the domestic grade market failed to move from established trading ranges set this morning. Jan West Texas Intermediate/Cushing was around 40 cents higher from Wednesday at $25.15-25 a barrel.
